questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The subject offer were very important to check out before choosing a specific university. As well as the location, perhaps the prices and if this destination is even cooperating with erasmus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you make friends at the university, it will be a very nice experience, tho does it requiere some patience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Communicating with the university back home was very bad, they wouldn't reply in weeks.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance of the erasmus office that was in the faculty,  but also assistance from spanish students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were very fast at responding an email, the office was also accesable all the time.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fortunately i had a friend from back home, that knew someone, that had an airbnb

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Especially in Madrid, a capital city, it is very hard to find an accommodation, so it would be best to live with other students but also to look for it a good time before the erasmus stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I don't know anything about it, since we got an apartment straight away. 
But i know many students that have struggled with that.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A lot of things went through "Mobility-online" , other than that you just needed to go to the eramus office and get a paper signed, Than you can also get the student id.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail, instagram page, facebook page and erasmus office which is available in each faculty

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult finding classes that matched with the times, so you would end up taking classes you don't want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To check out if they match time wise with each other.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You need to have a spanish level of C1, so the language level is very high, the teachers speak very fast

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching at Madrid University was a lot different than what im used to back home. 
The teachers are way more stricter, the expectation to the students were higher. My experience with some professors in Madrid were unpleasant. Although i do like that going to Uni is a bit more serious than in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Modern Greek, German, Spanish grammar, Analisys of discourse, Sociolinguistics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I only took these courses due to my personal interests, so its hard recommending these to future exchange students. Maybe spanish translation or something that has to do with spanish.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: 450 kr because of a broken lamp at home

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying groceries were much more expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I played football every tuesday with the erasmus students, but they offered many other sports such as ; volleyball, basketball

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The erasmus association had events almost every single day.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the non - academic activities that Erasmus has to offer, there you can meet many new people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to see other cities near by or explore the city as much as possible

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: At university it was a bit hard in the beginning, because all spanish students just looked at you like you were just an exchange student and didn't want to talk with you. This gets much better during the time

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Going up to them, being funny, because at the end we all have been there

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Definitely the fact that everyone is friends with everyone in uni and everyone hangs out together

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To be aware of the process of finding courses, being aware that  it takes some time before you are all settled in and to find a good and cheap accomendation beforehand.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember all your papers.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people and experience that i've made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam phase

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
